drafts.subject: chr:entity:mark-antony

time.source_expression: When it had been decided to deliver a sea battle

qualifierQuotations.text: When it had been decided to deliver a sea battle

drafts.quotation: Antony burned all the Egyptian ships except sixty; but the largest and best, from those having three to those having ten banks of oars, he manned
drafts.rationale: Antony decides which ships are kept or burned and mans the chosen ones, which shows supreme authority over the fleet he assembled for the sea battle. The passage ties this to the decision to fight at sea, so the fleet is identified with Antony's fleet at Actium.
drafts.relevance: It shows Antony's authority over the fleet assembled for the sea battle at Actium.

drafts.subject: chr:entity:publius-canidius-crassus
drafts.quotation: after Canidius their general had run away by night and forsaken the camp
drafts.rationale: Canidius is called 'their general' in reference to Antony's soldiers who held the camp, so he is identified as the general of Antony's land army. The passage shows him as its general, but only as he abandons it.
drafts.relevance: It shows who held formal command over Antony's land army at Actium when it was abandoned after the battle.
ambiguities: The passage gives no time for his tenure and shows him deserting after the naval battle, not directing the army in action.
